name: NG exhaustion chain phase-1 discovery protocol

phase_separation.phase1_goal: Discover how many sequential aftermath links carry out-of-sample predictive dependence and whether deeper dependence belongs to the same origin or behaves like a fresh first-order restart.
phase_separation.phase2_only: After phase-1 chain depth/boundaries are frozen, characterize the discovered chain instances using the forbidden fields above and any other legal contextual characteristics.

sparse_sensitivity.role: sensitivity check for omitted-state effects; cannot override the primary full-path result

validation.outer: leave-one-trading-week-out; every scored event is predicted only by models fit on the other two weeks
validation.inner: for each outer split and lag depth, choose model hyperparameters by alternating the two training weeks as train/validation; no outer-test tuning
validation.lag_semantics: D=1 asks whether the immediately prior aftermath predicts the current aftermath over an unconditional model. D=2 asks whether adding the aftermath two events back improves beyond D=1. D=3 asks whether the origin three events back still adds beyond the two more recent aftermaths, and so on.

models.ridge: linear multi-output ridge; alpha chosen from a fixed log grid by inner week validation
models.knn: nonlinear distance-weighted KNN multi-output regressor; k chosen from a fixed support grid by inner week validation
models.extra_trees: nonlinear tree ensemble; min_samples_leaf chosen from a fixed support grid by inner week validation

chain_evidence_rules.aggregate_confirmed_depth: A lag depth is confirmed only if its incremental outer-test loss improvement over D-1 has the same beneficial sign on all three weeks and across all three model families on the primary full-path vector.
chain_evidence_rules.aggregate_candidate_depth: If two of three model families improve on all three weeks but the third does not, preserve the depth as a candidate/sensitivity finding, not a frozen chain link.
chain_evidence_rules.origin_lineage_test: For each origin and depth D, compute the out-of-sample per-instance loss improvement from adding exactly that oldest origin aftermath. Test whether D=1 positive lineage makes D=2 positive lineage more likely than expected from their marginal rates. Repeat D=2->D=3. A true inherited chain should show positive cross-depth association; population-level memory without positive association is treated as restart/re-origin behavior rather than one continuous chain.

stop_rule: Continue lag depth until confirmed incremental improvement disappears. After two successive unconfirmed depths, deeper depths may be reported only as sensitivity and cannot define phase-1 chain boundaries without a new preregistered test.
